turns.text: quick q. need to fix my week for studying. missed subnetting questions AGAIN this morning on the practice app. ugh. i did a few chapters of the tabbed study guide (secondhand one) before work too and it still didn't stick

Subnetting usually needs short, repeated drills more than long reading sessions. To build a schedule I need your constraints. What are your work hours, and what other fixed commitments do you have each week?
i start at 2pm and get home after 10:30 mon-fri. also i train a new hire tue/thu 3-5pm so those are gone. iris leaves for work early so mornings are quiet at home. weekends are open too

Mornings before your 2 p.m. start are your best window, and Iris being out early means no interruptions. Here's a plan:

**Mon-Fri mornings (about 60-75 min)**
- 10 min: write out powers of 2 and the subnet mask table from memory
- 30-40 min: subnetting drills only (10 problems, work them by hand)
- 15 min: port number flashcards (the common ones: 22, 25, 53, 67/68, 80, 443, 3389)
- Use the practice-test app last, as a 10-question check

**Tue/Thu**
Keep the morning block as is. Don't try to study after 10:30 p.m.; you'll be tired and it won't stick. Skip those nights entirely.

**Mon/Wed/Fri evenings**
Only a 10-minute review of the morning's missed problems on your break or when you get home, if you feel like it.

**Weekends**
One longer session (90 min) on a timed practice test, then spend the rest of the time on the questions you missed, noting why each one went wrong.

Track your misses in a simple tally: subnetting vs. ports vs. other. After two weeks you'll see whether the gap is closing.

- Mornings Mon-Fri: 60 min. Powers of 2 + mask table, 10 hand-worked subnetting problems, 15 min port flashcards, then a 10-question app check
- Tue/Thu: same morning block, nothing after work
- Evenings: optional 10-min review of missed problems
- Weekend: one 90-min timed practice test + review every miss
- Keep a tally of misses by topic and check it after 2 weeks
